g.text: I2C-advanced — the combined-format transaction, field by field
START (SDA falls while SCL is high)
WRITE PHASE — arbitrary length, which is what makes the repeated START a real test
tHD;STA 6 ticks, then tLOW 7 ticks again
READ PHASE — a burst, so the master must DRIVE SDA again
ACK — master holds SDA low on cell 8
NACK — SDA released, the burst ends
no read byte is clocked at all; STOP, dmem[15] = 0x55
STOP (SDA rises while SCL is high)
THE BURST IS THE POINT. Continuing a read means pulling SDA LOW on the 9th
clock of every byte but the last, which is transmitter behaviour inside a
receive phase. A master that only ever releases SDA deadlocks here: the
slave waits for a byte nobody promises. The TB's slave counts what it
served (3) and what the master ACKed (2), and flags an ACK past the end.
THE RECIPIENT OF THE 9th CLOCK SWAPS BY PHASE.
address / write-data byte : the SLAVE drives cell 8
read byte : the MASTER drives cell 8
Nothing in the RTL knows which protocol is running; the state number is the
only thing that decides who owns the ninth clock.
